advances: For every whole-label reflected family covered by accepted fact `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd`, this theorem gives an exact quotient affine-selection alternative. Small hinge defect produces an actual reflected cloud whose continuous residual rank is at most \(\dim W\), with the sharp coefficient furnished by the accepted \(2\gamma_d\) domination. The exact attained Fenchel dual of the same defect is a \(W^\perp\)-valued stress already carried by the direct endpoint edges; it has exact force and affine-moment balance, feasible endpoint support load, and an objective realized by actual reflected metronoid contacts. The theorem deliberately stops before any identification with \(M_{\mathrm{off}}\) or any terminal capacity.

proof:
We first record the elementary geometry behind the quotient gauges. Fix \(y\in Z_+\), abbreviate \(K=C_y\), \(a=a_y\), and \(c=c_y\), and let
\[
 \Gamma:=\int_K(x-c)(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\,dx.
\tag{26}
\]
The matrix \(\Gamma\) is positive definite: if \(t\neq0\), then the nonnegative function \(\langle t,x-c\rangle^2\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on the positive-volume convex set \(K\). For every sufficiently small \(t\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 f_t(x):=\frac12+\langle t,x-c\rangle
\tag{27}
\]
lies in \([0,1]\) on \(K\), has integral \(a/2\), and has normalized first moment
\[
 \frac2a\int_Kx f_t(x)\,dx
 =c+\frac2a\Gamma t.
\tag{28}
\]
Thus \(L_y\) contains a neighborhood of \(c_y\). The density set defining \(L_y\) is convex and weak-* compact, so \(L_y\) is compact and convex. If a density \(f\) represents \(p\in L_y\), then \(1-f\) represents \(2c_y-p\); hence \(D_y=L_y-c_y\) is origin-symmetric. It follows that every \(B_\sigma\) is a full-dimensional compact convex origin-symmetric body in \(\mathbb R^d\). Therefore \(\bar B_\sigma\) has nonempty interior in \(V\). This includes \(V=\{0\}\), where its relative interior is \(\{0\}\). Consequently the gauges in (9) are finite and continuous, except that on the zero space they are simply zero. No strict convexity, smoothness, or uniqueness of supporting points is used.

Assume first that \(\Sigma\neq\varnothing\). Let \(A:=\operatorname{aff}\{m_\sigma\}\), and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq V^\Sigma\) be the finite-dimensional linear subspace
\[
 \mathcal L:=\{(\bar s(m_\sigma))_\sigma:
 \bar s:A\to V\text{ affine}\}.
\tag{29}
\]
Because all quotient gauges are equivalent to norms on \(V\), the objective in (10), viewed as a function of the evaluation tuple in \(\mathcal L\), tends to infinity when that tuple tends to infinity. Its sublevel sets in \(\mathcal L\) are therefore compact, so the minimum in (10) is attained. If \(V=\{0\}\), the same conclusion is immediate.

Choose an attaining \(\bar s\), and define \(\mathscr G\) by (12). Every label outside \(\mathscr G\) contributes more than \(\eta_\sigma/2\) to (10). Hence
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\in\mathscr G}\eta_\sigma
 \geq P-2\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}.
\tag{30}
\]
For \(\sigma\in\mathscr G\), the definition of the gauge and closedness of \(\bar B_\sigma\) give a point \(b_\sigma\in B_\sigma\) such that
\[
 \pi(b_\sigma)=
 \bar q_\sigma-\bar s(m_\sigma).
\tag{31}
\]
Put \(p_\sigma:=q_\sigma-b_\sigma\). Since \(B_\sigma=-B_\sigma\), one has \(p_\sigma\in K_\sigma\). Choose a linear right inverse of \(\pi\) and thereby an affine lift \(s:A\to\mathbb R^d\) of \(\bar s\). Equations (31) and \(p_\sigma=q_\sigma-b_\sigma\) give
\[
 p_\sigma-s(m_\sigma)\in W
 \qquad(\sigma\in\mathscr G).
\tag{32}
\]

The restriction of the label family to \(\mathscr G\) still satisfies the occurrence cap (5). Accepted fact `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd`, applied to the simultaneous choices \(p_\sigma\in K_\sigma\), proves (13) and support in the mixed-integer body. If the good-label mass is positive, apply the dominated-measure residual theorem in accepted fact `be359f8a6c628483` to the measure on the left side of (13). Let \(\rho_{\mathscr G}\) and \(r_{\mathscr G}\) be its intrinsic base and continuous residual ranks. Equation (32) gives \(r_{\mathscr G}\leq k\), while \(\rho_{\mathscr G}\leq n\). Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D
 &\geq
 2\gamma_d\,2^{n-\rho_{\mathscr G}}
 \frac{\sum_{\sigma\in\mathscr G}\eta_\sigma}
      {r_{\mathscr G}+1}\\
 &\geq
 \frac{2\gamma_d}{k+1}
 \bigl(P-2\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}\bigr)_+.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
If the good-label mass is zero, the right side of (33) is zero by (30), so the same conclusion is trivial. This proves (11)-(13); (14) follows from \(k+1\leq4\). The coefficient \(2\gamma_d\) in (33) is exactly the strongest coefficient supplied by the half-metronoid and quarter-cap accounting in `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd`.

We next prove the dual formula. For a full-dimensional compact convex origin-symmetric body \(B\) in a finite-dimensional vector space, the polar formula for its gauge is
\[
 \|x\|_B=\max_{h_B(w)\leq1}\langle w,x\rangle.
\tag{34}
\]
Consequently, for every \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \eta\left(\|x\|_B-\frac12\right)_+
 =\max_{h_B(v)\leq\eta}
 \left(\langle v,x\rangle-\frac12h_B(v)\right).
\tag{35}
\]
Indeed, write \(v=t w\) with \(0\leq t\leq\eta\) and \(h_B(w)=1\), with \(v=0\) treated separately, and maximize first over \(w\) and then over \(t\). Formula (35) is also valid on the zero vector space, where both sides vanish.

Let
\[
 F((x_\sigma)_\sigma):=
 \sum_\sigma\eta_\sigma
 \left(\|x_\sigma\|_{\bar B_\sigma}-\frac12\right)_+.
\tag{36}
\]
Formula (35) says that the convex conjugate of the \(\sigma\)-summand is
\[
 v\longmapsto
 \frac12h_{\bar B_\sigma}(v)
 +I_{\{h_{\bar B_\sigma}(v)\leq\eta_\sigma\}}(v).
\tag{37}
\]
The function \(F\) is finite and continuous on \(V^\Sigma\). Fenchel duality for minimizing \(F(\bar q-a)\) over the linear subspace \(a\in\mathcal L\) therefore has no gap and gives
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}
 =\max_{v\in\mathcal L^\perp}
 \sum_\sigma
 \left(
  \langle v_\sigma,\bar q_\sigma\rangle
  -\frac12h_{\bar B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)
 \right),
\tag{38}
\]
subject also to \(h_{\bar B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)\leq\eta_\sigma\). The feasible set is compact because each \(\bar B_\sigma\) has interior in \(V\), so the maximum is attained. Under the identification \(V^*=W^\perp\),
\[
 \langle v_\sigma,\bar q_\sigma\rangle
 =\langle v_\sigma,q_\sigma\rangle,
 \qquad
 h_{\bar B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)=h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma).
\tag{39}
\]

It remains to identify \(\mathcal L^\perp\). A tuple \((v_\sigma)\) annihilates every affine evaluation tuple if and only if
\[
 \sum_\sigma v_\sigma=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_\sigma v_\sigma m_\sigma^{\mathsf T}=0.
\tag{40}
\]
Necessity follows by testing constant maps and restrictions to \(A\) of ambient linear maps. Conversely, every affine map on \(A\) extends to \(\mathbb R^n\), and (40) annihilates such an extension. Substituting (39)-(40) into (38) proves (16), including all quotient and zero-dimensional cases.

Now fix a maximizer. The occurrence identity \(\sum_yN_{\sigma,y}=2\), valid also for loops, and (16) give
\[
 \sum_yU_y
 =\frac12\sum_\sigma\left(\sum_yN_{\sigma,y}\right)v_\sigma
 =\sum_\sigma v_\sigma=0,
\tag{41}
\]
and, using \(u_\sigma+v_\sigma=2m_\sigma\),
\[
 \sum_yU_yy^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac12\sum_\sigma
 v_\sigma(u_\sigma+v_\sigma)^{\mathsf T}
 =\sum_\sigma v_\sigma m_\sigma^{\mathsf T}=0.
\tag{42}
\]
Every \(U_y\) is in \(W^\perp\). Symmetry of \(D_y\) makes each support function nonnegative. For every occurrence of \(y\) in \(\sigma\),
\[
 \frac12h_{D_y}(v_\sigma)
 \leq\frac12\left(
 h_{D_{u_\sigma}}(v_\sigma)
 +h_{D_{v_\sigma}}(v_\sigma)
 \right)
 =h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)
 \leq\eta_\sigma.
\tag{43}
\]
Subadditivity and positive homogeneity of \(h_{D_y}\), followed by (43) and the multiplicity convention in (5), prove (19).

Compactness gives support maximizers in (20)-(21), including when \(v_\sigma=0\). Since \(D_y\) is convex and origin-symmetric, \(-d/2\in D_y\) for every \(d\in D_y\); hence (22) holds. Also
\[
 \frac{d_{\sigma,u}+d_{\sigma,v}}2\in B_\sigma,
\]
so (23) gives \(r_\sigma\in q_\sigma+B_\sigma=K_\sigma\). The support function of a Minkowski sum satisfies
\[
 h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)
 =\frac12\left(
 h_{D_{u_\sigma}}(v_\sigma)
 +h_{D_{v_\sigma}}(v_\sigma)
 \right).
\tag{44}
\]
Equations (21), (23), and (44) therefore give, label by label,
\[
 \langle v_\sigma,r_\sigma\rangle
 =\langle v_\sigma,q_\sigma\rangle
 -\frac12h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma).
\tag{45}
\]
Summing (45) and using dual optimality proves (24). Finally, the full label family satisfies (5), and every \(r_\sigma\in K_\sigma\). Accepted fact `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd` applied to these simultaneous choices proves (25) and the asserted mixed-integer support, including loops and all collisions.

Nothing in accepted facts `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd` or `be359f8a6c628483` makes the contact measure in (25) an admissible \(M_{\mathrm{off}}\) measure or charges the signed objective (24) to a terminal capacity. The final limitation in the statement is therefore part of the exact interface proved here, not an omitted inference.

If \(\Sigma=\varnothing\), the unique empty families give \(P=\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=0\), all displayed balances and domination statements are vacuous, and every conclusion follows.
statement:
Let \(n,d\geq1\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body, and use the fiber notation
\[
 C_y:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(y,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_y:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y),
 \qquad
 Z_+:=\{y\in\mathbb Z^n:a_y>0\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 \gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
 \qquad
 D:=2^n h_{\max}(C),
\tag{2}
\]
where, for every closed halfspace \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\),
\[
 \mu_C(H):=\sum_{y\in\mathbb Z^n}
 \operatorname{vol}_d\{x\in C_y:(y,x)\in H\},
 \qquad
 h_{\max}(C):=
 \sup_{p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}
 \inf_{\substack{H\ {\rm closed\ halfspace}\\p\in H}}\mu_C(H),
\]
as in accepted fact `be359f8a6c628483`. For a positive-volume convex body
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(0<t\leq\operatorname{vol}_d(K)\), use
\[
 \mathsf M_t(K):=
 \left\{
  \frac1t\int_Kx f(x)\,dx:
  f\in L^\infty(K),\ 0\leq f\leq1\ {\rm a.e.},\
  \int_Kf(x)\,dx=t
 \right\}.
\]
For \(y\in Z_+\), let
\[
 c_y:=\frac1{a_y}\int_{C_y}x\,dx,
 \qquad
 L_y:=\mathsf M_{a_y/2}(C_y),
 \qquad
 D_y:=L_y-c_y.
\tag{3}
\]
This is the metronoid normalization in accepted fact `ff5bc0ba02cc86cd`. Thus \(D_y\) is a compact convex origin-symmetric body.

Let \(\Sigma\) be a finite set of labels. Give each \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) a weight \(\eta_\sigma>0\) and two endpoint occurrences \(u_\sigma,v_\sigma\in Z_+\) such that
\[
 u_\sigma\equiv v_\sigma\pmod 2.
\tag{4}
\]
Occurrences are counted with multiplicity, including loops, and assume
\[
 \ell_y:=\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\eta_\sigma
 \bigl(\mathbf1_{\{u_\sigma=y\}}+
       \mathbf1_{\{v_\sigma=y\}}\bigr)
 \leq\frac{a_y}{4}
 \qquad(y\in Z_+).
\tag{5}
\]
For each label put
\[
 m_\sigma:=\frac{u_\sigma+v_\sigma}{2}\in\mathbb Z^n,
 \qquad
 q_\sigma:=\frac{c_{u_\sigma}+c_{v_\sigma}}2,
\tag{6}
\]
\[
 B_\sigma:=\frac{D_{u_\sigma}+D_{v_\sigma}}2,
 \qquad
 K_\sigma:=q_\sigma+B_\sigma
 =\frac{L_{u_\sigma}+L_{v_\sigma}}2,
 \qquad
 P:=\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\eta_\sigma.
\tag{7}
\]

Fix a linear subspace \(W\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) of dimension \(k\), let \(\pi:\mathbb R^d\to V:=\mathbb R^d/W\) be the quotient map, and write
\[
 \bar q_\sigma:=\pi(q_\sigma),
 \qquad
 \bar B_\sigma:=\pi(B_\sigma).
\tag{8}
\]
The quotient gauge is
\[
 \|x\|_{\bar B_\sigma}:=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in t\bar B_\sigma\}.
\tag{9}
\]
This convention includes the zero-dimensional quotient: if \(V=\{0\}\), then \(\bar B_\sigma=\{0\}\) and its gauge is zero. Define the reflected quotient hinge defect
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}:=
 \min_{\bar s:\operatorname{aff}\{m_\sigma:\sigma\in\Sigma\}\to V
                 \ \mathrm{affine}}
 \sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\eta_\sigma
 \left(
  \|\bar q_\sigma-\bar s(m_\sigma)\|_{\bar B_\sigma}
  -\frac12
 \right)_+.
\tag{10}
\]
For \(\Sigma=\varnothing\), set \(P=\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=0\). The minimum in (10) is attained.

The following small-defect conclusion holds:
\[
 \boxed{
 D\geq
 \frac{2\gamma_d}{k+1}
 \bigl(P-2\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}\bigr)_+.
 }
\tag{11}
\]
More precisely, an attaining \(\bar s\) and the good-label set
\[
 \mathscr G:=\left\{\sigma:
 \|\bar q_\sigma-\bar s(m_\sigma)\|_{\bar B_\sigma}\leq1
 \right\}
\tag{12}
\]
admit simultaneous points \(p_\sigma\in K_\sigma\), \(\sigma\in\mathscr G\), for which
\[
 2\gamma_d\sum_{\sigma\in\mathscr G}
 \eta_\sigma\delta_{(m_\sigma,p_\sigma)}
 \preceq_{\mathrm{hs}}\mu_C,
\tag{13}
\]
and the continuous residual rank of this measure in the sense of `be359f8a6c628483` is at most \(k\). In particular, if \(k\leq3\), then
\[
 \boxed{
 D\geq\frac{\gamma_d}{2}
 \bigl(P-2\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}\bigr)_+.
 }
\tag{14}
\]

Identify \(V^*\) with \(W^\perp\) by
\(\langle v,\pi(x)\rangle:=\langle v,x\rangle\). For a compact convex set \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), write
\[
 h_B(v):=\max_{b\in B}\langle v,b\rangle.
\tag{15}
\]
Then (10) has the exact attained dual
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=\max\quad&
 \sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \left(
  \langle v_\sigma,q_\sigma\rangle
  -\frac12h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)
 \right)\\
 \text{subject to}\quad&
 v_\sigma\in W^\perp,\\
 &h_{B_\sigma}(v_\sigma)\leq\eta_\sigma,\\
 &\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}v_\sigma=0,\\
 &\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 v_\sigma m_\sigma^{\mathsf T}=0.
 \end{aligned}}
\tag{16}
\]
The zero family is feasible, and the maximum is attained even when \(W=\mathbb R^d\), in which case both sides of (16) are zero.

Let \((v_\sigma)\) be any maximizer in (16), and set
\[
 N_{\sigma,y}:=
 \mathbf1_{\{u_\sigma=y\}}+
 \mathbf1_{\{v_\sigma=y\}},
 \qquad
 U_y:=\frac12\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 N_{\sigma,y}v_\sigma.
\tag{17}
\]
Then the direct-edge endpoint collapse satisfies
\[
 U_y\in W^\perp,
 \qquad
 \sum_yU_y=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_yU_yy^{\mathsf T}=0,
\tag{18}
\]
and the pointwise support-load bound
\[
 \boxed{
 h_{D_y}(U_y)
 \leq\frac12\sum_\sigma
 N_{\sigma,y}h_{D_y}(v_\sigma)
 \leq\ell_y
 \leq\frac{a_y}{4}.
 }
\tag{19}
\]

Finally, for every \(\sigma\), there are
\[
 d_{\sigma,u}\in D_{u_\sigma},
 \qquad
 d_{\sigma,v}\in D_{v_\sigma}
\tag{20}
\]
such that
\[
 \langle v_\sigma,d_{\sigma,u}\rangle
 =h_{D_{u_\sigma}}(v_\sigma),
 \qquad
 \langle v_\sigma,d_{\sigma,v}\rangle
 =h_{D_{v_\sigma}}(v_\sigma).
\tag{21}
\]
Define the reflected endpoint contacts and their midpoint by
\[
 x_{\sigma,u}:=c_{u_\sigma}-\frac12d_{\sigma,u}\in L_{u_\sigma},
 \qquad
 x_{\sigma,v}:=c_{v_\sigma}-\frac12d_{\sigma,v}\in L_{v_\sigma},
\tag{22}
\]
\[
 r_\sigma:=\frac{x_{\sigma,u}+x_{\sigma,v}}2
 =q_\sigma-\frac14(d_{\sigma,u}+d_{\sigma,v})
 \in K_\sigma.
\tag{23}
\]
They realize the dual objective exactly:
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}
 =\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \langle v_\sigma,r_\sigma\rangle.
 }
\tag{24}
\]
Moreover, the actual reflected-contact measure satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 2\gamma_d\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \eta_\sigma\delta_{(m_\sigma,r_\sigma)}
 \preceq_{\mathrm{hs}}\mu_C,
 }
\tag{25}
\]
and every \((m_\sigma,r_\sigma)\) belongs to
\(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), with multiplicities retained under collisions.

No assertion identifies (25), the contact objective (24), or the forces (17) with \(M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)\), and no inequality from \(\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}\) to an existing terminal capacity is claimed. In particular, this theorem is not a proof of the weak Oertel conjecture.
